instrument.v: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8)
instrument.label: Verified fact

issuer.v: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, OCC and FDIC (interagency)
issuer.label: Verified fact

status_and_dates.v: Issued 17 April 2026. Supersedes and replaces SR 11-7 (4 April 2011) and SR 21-8 (9 April 2021); OCC rescinded Bulletins 2011-12, 1997-24 and 2021-19 and the Comptroller's Handbook 'Model Risk Management' booklet. Expected to be most relevant to banking organisations with over US$30 billion in total assets. Generative AI and agentic AI models are expressly outside its scope; the agencies said they plan to issue 'in the near future' a request for information on model risk management and banks' use of AI including generative and agentic AI. No such RFI was found published as of 7 October 2026.
status_and_dates.label: Verified fact

v: Model defined as 'a complex quantitative method, system, or approach that applies statistical, economic, or financial theories to process input data into quantitative estimates'; excludes simple arithmetic and deterministic rule-based software without such theories
Risk-based, materiality-driven MRM scaled to model risk profile, size and complexity; immaterial models identified and monitored for change in materiality
Effective challenge by qualified, independent reviewers; model risk assessed individually and in aggregate
Principles apply to traditional statistical and quantitative models and non-generative, non-agentic AI models
For tools, processes or systems not covered (including GenAI and agentic AI), the firm's own risk management and governance practices should determine governance and controls
Not enforceable in itself, but supervisory action may follow violations of law or unsafe or unsound practices stemming from insufficient management of model risk
key_obligations.label: Verified fact

relevance_to_genai_agents_asset_mgmt.v: For an asset manager with US exposure, SR 26-2 is not directly binding unless it is part of a US banking organisation, but US bank-owned managers and counterparties will use it as the reference MRM standard. The explicit GenAI/agentic carve-out removes the 'is an LLM a model?' debate for US banks only by deferring it; firms still need their own governance for LLM-based agents, and the AI RFI may reintroduce expectations. Architecture should therefore keep MRM-grade inventory, versioning and monitoring for LLM components regardless of scope.
relevance_to_genai_agents_asset_mgmt.label: Architectural judgement

v: Model inventory with materiality/tiering
Independent validation and effective-challenge records for in-scope models
Ongoing monitoring evidence and materiality re-assessment
Documented governance for out-of-scope GenAI/agentic tools under the firm's own risk framework
evidence_artefacts_expected.label: Reported

stage_a_notes: Sources differ on 'SR 26-2' vs 'SR 26-02' and on 'revision' vs 'replacement'; the Fed letter says 'supersedes and replaces'. Full attachment text not read (occ.gov and federalreserve.gov blocked); validation and documentation detail rests on search extracts. The OCC 2022 testimony that many AI tools would be considered models contrasts with the 2026 carve-out (reported in search extract, not archived).

instrument.v: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
instrument.label: Verified fact

jurisdiction.v: European Union (extraterritorial: providers placing on EU market, deployers in the EU)
jurisdiction.label: Reported

issuer.v: European Parliament and Council; enforced by the AI Office (GPAI) and Member State authorities
issuer.label: Verified fact

status_and_dates.v: Entered into force 1 August 2024 (reported). Prohibitions and AI literacy apply from 2 February 2025. GPAI obligations and governance from 2 August 2025; Commission enforcement powers over GPAI (fines up to 3% of global turnover) from 2 August 2026; GPAI models placed before 2 August 2025 must comply by 2 August 2027. Article 50 transparency applies from 2 August 2026 (Article 50(2) marking: systems already on the market have until 2 December 2026). Under the Digital Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, OJ 24 July 2026, in force 27 July 2026), Annex III stand-alone high-risk obligations moved from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 and Annex I (product-embedded) high-risk obligations to 2 August 2028; new prohibitions (non-consensual intimate imagery, CSAM generation) apply from 2 December 2026.
status_and_dates.label: Verified fact

v: Article 4 AI literacy (as amended 27 July 2026): providers and deployers take measures to support AI literacy of staff; no guarantee of a specific level for any individual
Article 5 prohibited practices

Article 26 deployers of high-risk systems: use per instructions; competent human oversight; relevant and representative input data where controlled; keep logs at least six months (financial institutions within financial-services documentation); monitor operation and inform provider; suspend and notify on risk; report serious incidents; inform workers and affected persons

Article 25: a deployer becomes a provider if it rebrands, substantially modifies a high-risk system, or changes the intended purpose of an AI system (including a GPAI system) so that it becomes high-risk
Article 27: fundamental rights impact assessment by deployers of Annex III 5(b) and 5(c) systems

Article 50: providers disclose AI interaction (chatbots) and mark synthetic output machine-readably; deployers disclose deep fakes and AI-generated public-interest text unless human-reviewed with editorial responsibility

Articles 53/55: GPAI providers keep technical documentation, inform downstream providers, copyright policy, training-content summary; systemic-risk models (presumed above 10^25 FLOP) add evaluations, adversarial testing, incident reporting, cybersecurity
Article 72: providers of high-risk systems run a documented post-market monitoring system and plan, collecting performance data over the lifetime including from deployers

Annex III relevant to financial services: 4(a)/(b) employment and worker management; 5(b) creditworthiness and credit scoring (fraud detection excluded); 5(c) risk assessment and pricing for natural persons in life and health insurance
key_obligations.label: Verified fact

relevance_to_genai_agents_asset_mgmt.v: An asset manager using third-party LLMs is normally a deployer, not a GPAI provider; GPAI obligations sit with the model vendor. Most asset-management use cases (research summaries, performance-attribution commentary, operations) are not in Annex III, so the main live duties are AI literacy, Article 50 transparency for client-facing chat or published content, and prohibitions. HR use (Annex III point 4) and any credit or life/health insurance pricing would be high-risk from 2 December 2027. Fine-tuning or repurposing a model into a high-risk purpose can make the firm a provider (Article 25). Logging duties for financial institutions fold into existing financial-services record-keeping.
relevance_to_genai_agents_asset_mgmt.label: Architectural judgement

v: AI inventory with risk classification per use case (prohibited / high-risk / Article 50 / minimal)
AI literacy programme records
Article 50 disclosures and synthetic-content marking evidence
For any high-risk deployment: instructions-for-use adherence, human-oversight assignments, logs kept six months or more, monitoring and incident records, FRIA for 5(b)/5(c)
Supplier documentation from GPAI providers (Article 53 downstream information)
evidence_artefacts_expected.label: Verified fact

stage_a_notes: Conflict: one search extract read amended Article 4 as obliging providers and deployers; commentary (A8-S013) says the Omnibus softened Article 4 to an obligation of means and added Commission/Member State support duties. EUR-Lex not directly readable. Sources also disagree on the Omnibus signature date (8 July 2026 vs adoption dates 16/29 June 2026); publication 24 July 2026 and entry into force 27 July 2026 are consistent across Commission and EUR-Lex extracts. One extract notes a source conflict on the post-market monitoring template deadline; the Omnibus removed the Commission's power to adopt the Article 72(3) template.
